chapter: Looking back: rock, blues, childhood and guitar innovators
title: Eddie Durham, Charlie Christian and Oscar Moore
summary: He credits Durham as an early guitarist and Christian's exciting style, but says Oscar Moore thought like him harmonically before quitting playing.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Who were the Early innovators on guitar?
Who was the first one to establish the guitar in jazz?

In jazz, well I think that Eddy Durham in my opinion was one of the early ones. And then came Charlie Christian. And there is a guitarist that we just haven't mentioned at all, and I think that in his way -- he was as great as Charlie, but in a different way. Oscar Moore. Oscar Moore was a great guitarist. I had the utmost admiration for

Oscar Moore. But unfortunately -- not unfortunately, but at that time there was just two styles, and Charlie Christian had a more exciting style. Charlie played like a horn, you know. He was a driving guitarist, amazing technique and all this. But musically, when we come down to musically that Oscar Moore was -- he was just something else.
I felt -- well, he was one of the giants. Let's face it, he was one of the giants. So I kind of -- Oscar and I had more in common. I -- we thought -- Oscar and I thought alike.

Harmonically, yeah. Oscar and I, you know, we kind of thought alike. So we kind of gravitated toward eachother. Whe he'd come to town he would kind of seek me out, or if I was around him I would seek him out. And we would play and you know -- but when he left Nat he just -- it's an amazing thing. I think he stopped playing. Now, this I could never reconcile myself to this. How could a man who was that great just stop playing. You know. And he was comparatively -- at the point he stopped he was in his forties, wasn't he. I think he was in his forties.

Well, after he left Nat he went with his brother's group for a while, the Four Blazers. Johnny Moore's Four Blazers. But after that he just stopped. But he was a great guitarist, he was an innovator also. And let's see.
